Slack Events API + interactivity endpoint (handled by Bolt).

Bolt owns signature verification, the ``url_verification`` challenge,
per-workspace token resolution (via the custom ``authorize`` that
bridges to ``IntegrationToken``), and dispatch to the event / action
/ assistant listeners registered in ``app.integrations.slack_bolt_app``.
Point both the Slack *Events* and *Interactivity* Request URLs here.
Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

Inbound Bot Framework endpoint (Activities). JWT auth + dispatch.

The adapter validates the Bot-Framework JWT (the Teams analog of Slack's
signature check) inside ``process_activity``; we just deserialize the
Activity and hand it to the bot's ``on_turn``.
Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

Start the Teams connection: returns a pairing code (admin only).

The admin installs the Unisson Teams app, then messages the bot
``/connect <code>``; the bot claims the code and stores the tenant link.

Inbound Twilio WhatsApp webhook (form-encoded). Acks immediately.

Verifies ``X-Twilio-Signature``, dedups on ``MessageSid``, then either
completes a pending verification (the member echoed their code) or routes the
message to the bound member's org. Twilio retries on a slow response, so the
heavy turn runs in a background task.
Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

Inbound Postmark email webhook (JSON). Acks immediately.

Verifies the shared secret, enforces DMARC, dedups on ``Message-ID``, then
either completes a pending verification or routes the mail to the bound
member's org. Threads by the email's root ``Message-ID``.
Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

Whether the server is configured for each channel + this org's paired count.

"Configured" is derived from the credentials actually needed to operate —
there's no separate enable flag; each provider is always registered and
simply no-ops without these (like Slack without a token).

Import one or many Razorpay API key pairs (admin only).

Body shape:
    {
      "items": [
        {"key_id": "rzp_test_…", "key_secret": "…",
         "display_name": "Acme India PG", "label": "primary"},
        ...
      ]
    }

Each key's environment is derived from the ``key_id`` prefix and
each pair is probed via ``GET /v1/payments?count=1`` to confirm
validity. The admin-supplied ``display_name`` is the dedup key —
re-importing under the same name attaches the new pair to the
same account. Returns a per-item result so the UI can show
success / failure for each row independently.

can show success/failure for each line of the textarea independently.

Import one or many Mirakl API keys (admin only).

Body shape:
    {
      "items": [
        {"instance_url": "https://acme.mirakl.net", "persona": "operator",
         "api_key": "…", "label": "Acme operator"},
        ...
      ]
    }

Each key is validated against its instance URL with a persona-appropriate,
param-less GET, then stored encrypted in the org-level pool. There's no
per-key account — admins assign keys to users separately. Returns a per-item
result so the UI can show success/failure for each row independently.
